features.summary: A vendor: the data a component's declaration carries, in closed sets the one driver follows. Where the object lives, a path from the element or a lookup the vendor's code provides as a plugin; how a listener subscribes, a method pair, a callback property whose listeners chain on one framework function per object and property, or a subscribe method that returns its unsubscriber; where the object holds its element; what a listener receives, its arguments, with the payload at the place its event declares and the vendor's continuation called at its position; a callback the vendor calls for an answer, written as an expression; the vendor contract, which checks every declaration against the vendor's typed API at build; and the bridge to a component's own code: alis:mount and alis:unmount, announced over the content a boot, a slot's load or its unload covers, and the page's plugin queue, through which a vendor's code provides its lookup, read at boot before alis:mount, each later push registering at once. Main has no vendor data: its runtime holds a driver per vendor name, native and fusion, and reads Syncfusion's object by name. The redesign writes a vendor's path, listening and payload kind into the plan, with two listening kinds and a path alone; its payload kind, VendorEventPayload, leaves for the handler's payload place (D17.4).

meanings.meaning: A vendor name names one vendor: one place of the object (its path or its lookup), one listening and one element path. Two definitions of one name whose data differ are refused: at build by ALIS034 when both are constants of one compilation, and where the view renders when one plan names both, as the redesign refuses them.

features.oracle: The DOM Standard's EventTarget, addEventListener and removeEventListener, and CustomEvent's detail; ECMAScript's property assignment, call and Object.freeze, by which a vendor's object adds, assigns, refuses and removes a listener; and each vendor's typed API as TypeScript 5.9.3 types it (D17.5).

defects.defect: Two definitions of one vendor name with different data both render, so one plan's handlers find the object by another definition's path or listening, or the view throws only where both meet in one plan (M12.D1). ALIS034 (N18.12) reports two constant definitions of one name whose path, lookup, listening or element path differ in one compilation; where the view renders, a plan that names both is refused with "Two different vendors are named '{name}'. Give each vendor its own name." (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Writing/Scope.cs:270 at 65fdf118d).

A vendor's object path with an empty step, as "slate.", writes a path whose step names nothing, so every step that reaches the object stops in the browser. ALIS034 (N18.12) reports a constant object path or element path with an empty step; where the view renders on code it does not follow, the path is refused with "Path '{text}' contains an empty segment at index {index}. Use dot-separated property names without consecutive, leading, or trailing dots." (Alis.Reactive/WireTerms/Path.cs:124-125 at 65fdf118d).

promises.page: A ward door page whose door sensor is an element that is its own component (ComponentVendor.Native) and declares Opened, an Event<DoorSignal> whose payload is the event the sensor raises: DoorSignal declares Type, a ReadOnly<string>, and Detail, a ReadOnly<DoorOpened> of the app's class DoorOpened with a string Room. The sensor's button Open with room raises a CustomEvent named opened with the detail {"room": "12"}, and its button Open with no room raises opened with no detail. The Opened handler writes the payload's Type into opened-type and its Detail's Room into opened-room.
promises.gesture: Click Open with room, then Open with no room.
promises.outcome: After each click opened-type reads opened; after the first opened-room reads 12, and after the second it is empty.
promises.opposite: Click Open with room once more: opened-type reads opened and opened-room reads 12.
promises.defect: The payload follows the dispatch, not the declaration: the redesign hands the handler a CustomEvent's detail when it carries one and the event when it carries none (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/vendor-driver.ts:89-92 at 65fdf118d), so opened-type is empty after Open with room.

promises.page: A ward monitor page with oxygen gauges whose library keeps its gauges in a registry of its own, off their elements, found by the lookup the gauge's code provides as the plugin oxygen-gauges, named by VendorLookup.ByPlugin("oxygen-gauges") in the gauge's vendor. The gauge declares Reading, a ReadOnly<int>; Threshold, a Property<int> it shows; Lower() and Raise(), which show Alarm lowered and Alarm raised beside it; and Alarmed, an Event its button Sound the alarm raises. gauge-bed-1 is a gauge the library made with the reading 97; gauge-bed-2 is an element the library has made no gauge for, until the page's button Make the bed 2 gauge makes one with the reading 88. Read bed 1 writes gauge-bed-1's Reading into reading-1; Set the threshold to 92 writes 92 into gauge-bed-1's Threshold; Raise the alarm and Lower the alarm call gauge-bed-1's Raise() and Lower(); gauge-bed-1's Alarmed handler writes alarmed into alarm-heard; Read bed 2 writes reading into bed-2-tried, then gauge-bed-2's Reading into reading-2 and read into bed-2-done.
promises.gesture: Click Read bed 1, Set the threshold to 92, Raise the alarm, Lower the alarm and Sound the alarm; then click Read bed 2 and Raise the alarm.
promises.outcome: reading-1 reads 97, gauge bed 1 shows the threshold 92, alarm-heard reads alarmed, and gauge bed 1 shows Alarm lowered after Lower the alarm and Alarm raised after the last click; bed-2-tried reads reading, and reading-2 and bed-2-done are empty.
promises.opposite: Click Make the bed 2 gauge, then Read bed 2: reading-2 reads 88 and bed-2-done reads read, so the lookup runs when a step reaches the gauge.
promises.defect: The lookup is skipped or read once: a gauge kept off its element reads nothing and its alarm never moves, so reading-1 is empty; or a gauge the library never made reads nothing and the pipeline goes on, so bed-2-done reads read (D17.3, D4.1).

promises.page: A nurses' station page with a ward feed the app brings, whose declaration names its listening with ComponentVendor.DefineReturnedUnsubscriber("wardfeed", objectPath: "feed", subscribe: "subscribe") and declares Posted, an Event<FeedUpdate> with a string Message. The feed's button Post an update posts the message Bed 4 needs water, and the feed shows the count of listeners it holds as subscribers: n. The page's Posted handler writes the payload's Message into last-update. Open the feed card loads the slot feed-card with a partial whose plan, when it loads, listens to the feed's Posted, reached by its element's id, with a pipeline that adds one to the page's tally and writes it into card-heard, an element outside the slot; Close the feed card unloads it.
promises.gesture: Click Open the feed card, Post an update, Close the feed card, then Post an update.
promises.outcome: After the first Post an update, card-heard reads 1 and the feed shows subscribers: 2; after Close the feed card the feed shows subscribers: 1; after the second Post an update, card-heard still reads 1 and last-update reads Bed 4 needs water.
promises.opposite: Click Open the feed card and Post an update again: card-heard reads 2 and the feed shows subscribers: 2.
promises.defect: The release calls nothing, or a method named as the subscribe's pair, where the feed removes a listener only by the function its subscribe returned, so the feed keeps subscribers: 2 and the second Post an update writes 2 into card-heard.

promises.page: An admission page with a resident search box the app brings, whose Search event its vendor raises with two arguments, the typed query and the vendor's continuation, which shows each item it is handed as an option under the box. The payload's declaration declares Query, the first argument's text, and Show, the continuation, MethodAt(1, [items]). The Search handler writes Query into searched-for and calls Show with the page's list of residents, Ada Byrne and Adam Cole.
promises.gesture: Type Ad into the resident search box, and wait until searched-for reads Ad.
promises.outcome: searched-for reads Ad, and the box shows the options Ada Byrne and Adam Cole.
promises.opposite: Before any typing, the box shows no option and searched-for is empty.
promises.defect: The continuation at position 1 is not called, or is called with nothing, so the box shows no option; or Query reads an argument other than the first, so searched-for is empty (D17.4).

promises.page: A dose chart page with two charts the app brings, each of whose declaration declares TickLabel, a Callback<TickArgs, string> its vendor calls for each tick with the tick's Resident and draws the answer as the tick's label; a chart with no TickLabel draws each tick's position, 1, 2 and 3. Both charts hold the ticks Ada, Bea and Cy. The view sets chart-labeled's TickLabel to tick => tick.Resident and leaves chart-plain's unset; the page's button Draw the charts draws both.

promises.outcome: chart-labeled's ticks read Ada, Bea and Cy.
promises.opposite: chart-plain's ticks read 1, 2 and 3.
promises.defect: The answer is not the function the vendor calls, or answers nothing, so chart-labeled's ticks read 1, 2 and 3, or are empty (D17.12).

promises.page: A call bell page whose bell the app brings declares Rang, an Event<RingArgs> with a string Room, and Chimed, an Event with no payload. The bell's button Ring with no room raises rang with no argument, its button Ring room 7 raises rang with {"room": "7"}, and its button Chime raises chimed with no argument; after each raise the bell's own code writes its count of raises into raised. The Rang handler writes ringing into ring-tried as its first step, then the payload's Room into ring-room; the Chimed handler writes chimed into chime-heard.
promises.gesture: Click Ring with no room, then Chime.
promises.outcome: After Ring with no room, raised reads 1 and ring-tried and ring-room are empty; after Chime, chime-heard reads chimed and raised reads 2.
promises.opposite: Click Ring room 7: ring-tried reads ringing, ring-room reads 7 and raised reads 3.
promises.defect: The missing payload reads as nothing and the handler runs, so ring-tried reads ringing after Ring with no room, as the redesign reads a payload's members as optional (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Values/Target.cs:80 at 65fdf118d); or the stop reaches the vendor, so raised stays empty; or Chimed's empty payload stops it, so chime-heard is empty.

promises.page: A dose chart page with a text box unit-name, a shift clock the app brings whose Shift(), a Method<string>, answers Day until its button Next shift turns it to Night, and a chart the app brings that declares Caption and Footer, each a Callback<CaptionArgs, string> it calls at each draw and shows above and below its ticks, and SortTicks(Answer(key)), a Method that orders and redraws its ticks by the key its answer gives for each. promises.page: A nurses' station page with a call bell the app brings, whose declaration names its listening with ComponentVendor.DefineCallbackProperties("callbell", objectPath: "bell") and declares Rang, an Event<RingArgs> with a string Room, heard through the bell's onRang property; the bell's own code assigns onRang a function that appends bell to the ring log, and its button Ring room 7 rings with the room 7, each ring writing a new line into the ring log. features.summary: A component on the page: Component, the base of a component's declaration, a live object whose listening is its vendor's; IComponent, carrying the ComponentVendor a declaration names; plan.Render<TComponent>(id, markup), which writes the markup a render helper gives, and RenderedComponent's Reactive, a handler of a declared event from the plan's start, which names the element as that declaration's component in the plan; and pipeline.Component<TComponent>(id), the component on the element of that id, typed by its declaration. An element holds one component in a plan, and a handler whose element holds no object when its plan starts does not start and stops no other. Main's IComponent names its vendor by a string its runtime picks a driver by, and main reaches a component through ComponentRef, whose writes and calls are internal; the redesign carries the vendor as data and reaches a component as its declaration.

meanings.meaning: A handler of a component's event subscribes when its plan's owner starts, after alis:mount has announced the content that owner covers, at boot and at a slot's load alike. A handler whose element the page lacks, or whose element holds no object at its vendor's place, does not start and never starts later: the console shows one error naming the element and its vendor, and the plan's other handlers subscribe. A step that reaches that element when it runs finds the object then, and stops only its own pipeline when it is still missing (D4.1).

features.oracle: ASP.NET Core's IHtmlContent and MVC 5's IHtmlString, through which a view writes a component's markup, and the DOM Standard's getElementById, by which the runtime finds a component's element.

defects.defect: An element a plan names as the component of two vendors renders, so the plan finds one element's object by two vendors' places and listenings. Where the view renders it is refused with "Element '{id}' is named as a component of vendor '{first}' and as one of vendor '{second}', but an element holds one component: name it by the declaration of the component its view renders." (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Document/PlanBuildContext.cs:128-129 at 65fdf118d).

A handler whose element holds no object when its plan starts stops the plan's other handlers from subscribing, subscribes later to an object built after the start, or fails with no error naming it (M12.D2).

promises.page: A medication room page with a dose timer the app brings: its declaration, its render helper and its browser code are the app's own, and its code builds the timer on alis:mount. The timer shows its minutes and declares Minutes, a Property<int> that starts at 30; Restart(), a Method that sets the minutes back to 30; and Elapsed, an Event<TimerElapsed> with a string Resident, which the timer's button Let it elapse raises for the resident Ada. Read the minutes writes Minutes into minutes-read; Set 15 minutes writes 15 into Minutes; Restart calls Restart(); the Elapsed handler writes the payload's Resident into elapsed-for.
promises.gesture: Click Set 15 minutes and Read the minutes; click Restart and Read the minutes; click Let it elapse.
promises.outcome: After the first Read the minutes, minutes-read reads 15 and the timer shows 15; after the second, minutes-read reads 30 and the timer shows 30; after Let it elapse, elapsed-for reads Ada.
promises.opposite: Before any click, the timer shows 30, and minutes-read and elapsed-for are empty.
promises.defect: A step reaches only a component the framework's packages onboard, as main's runtime holds drivers for native and fusion alone (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/browser-objects/component-driver.ts:89-90 at 623dd4a27), so minutes-read, the timer's minutes or elapsed-for stays as it was.

The monitor's button Sound the alarm raises Alarmed, and its button Shut down destroys it and takes it off its element.
promises.gesture: Click Open the panel, Shut down, Close the panel, Open the panel, then Sound the alarm.
promises.outcome: alarm-heard reads alarm, and the console shows no error.

promises.page: A ward page whose slot bed-card, loaded by Open the card and unloaded by Close the card, renders a bed monitor the app brings; the card's plan has the monitor's Alarmed handler, which adds one to the page's tally and writes it into alarms-heard, an element outside the slot. The monitor's button Sound the alarm raises Alarmed, and its button Restart, the monitor's host, destroys it and puts a new monitor on the same element; every monitor's unsubscribe adds one to the page's count of calls in off-calls, and a monitor's destroy, by Restart or on alis:unmount, calls no unsubscribe.
promises.gesture: Click Open the card, Sound the alarm, Restart, Sound the alarm, then Close the card.
promises.outcome: alarms-heard reads 1, and off-calls reads 0 after Close the card.
promises.opposite: Without Restart, Close the card writes 1 into off-calls.
promises.defect: The handler follows the element to the new object, so alarms-heard reads 2; or the release calls the unsubscribe of the object the element holds now, so off-calls reads 1.

A built timer's button Let it elapse raises Elapsed.

verdicts.reason: A reach whose writes and calls are internal, EmitSet and EmitCall over a member named as a string (Alis.Reactive/Components/Contracts/ComponentRef.cs:31-65 at 623dd4a27), so only the framework's packages declare what a step does on a component, and a component an app brings has no door. The rewrite reaches a component as its declaration (M12.N2), whose members a step reads with Read (N5.6) and calls with any number of arguments (N5.3).

A vendor named by a string the runtime picks a driver by, native or fusion (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/browser-objects/component-driver.ts:89-90 at 623dd4a27), so the runtime names each vendor it serves. The rewrite carries the vendor as data the one driver follows (D17.3): IComponent.Vendor is the ComponentVendor a declaration names (M12.N1).
